adequacyEvidence.finding: Existing rules distinguish clocks, denominators, weighted/bias-limited counts and event opportunity. They already reject CPU-to-latency conversion and treating zero as absence.
Existing rule explicitly covers in-progress platform-thread park invisibility, avoids lowering thresholds as a false remedy and preserves recovery priority.
adequacyEvidence.technicalEvidence: Isolated JDK 25 test confirmed target event count 0 during park and 1 after return, with completed positive control in both artifacts.

adequacyEvidence.finding: Concurrent recording settings are already treated as combined, not file-local event filters; owned recording stop and unrelated capture preservation are explicit.
adequacyEvidence.sourceEvidence: JDK 25 Event.shouldCommit documents the minimum threshold across running recordings.

adequacyEvidence.finding: Existing commands are version/target-scoped, separate schema/format from event semantics, and diagnose attach/engine/access failures without default privilege escalation.

capabilitiesPreserved: All four package files byte-for-byte unchanged.

technicalEvaluation.classification: Executed isolated JVM/API behavior check; not an agent behavioral evaluation.
technicalEvaluation.expectedDefinedBeforeRun: Target ThreadPark count 0 while in progress, 1 after return; completed positive-control count 1 in both. A premature target return invalidates the run.
technicalEvaluation.controls: Completed same-event positive control; ongoing target is a counterexample to the zero-events-means-no-wait inference. Harness rejects premature park returns.
technicalEvaluation.scope: One platform-thread park in a bounded local process, using an explicit JFR event setting. No production attach, workload injection or async-profiler execution.

structuredWalkthroughs.result: Use existing live evidence and report commit-point visibility limit; no threshold reduction or forced completion.
Use recorded target duration for the completed event and stop unnecessary recapture; preserve scope and critical-path uncertainty.
